newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MAS gets nod to lift international fares.
newsitem.headline: MAS gets nod to lift international fares.

text.p: The Malaysian government has no objection if national carrier Malaysian Airline Systems Bhd (MAS) wants to raise its international fares, the Bernama news agency reported on Wednesday.
The International Air Traffic Association (IATA) has proposed a three percent increase in the fares of all global airlines.
Malaysian Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik said MAS was free follow IATA's proposal as long as domestic fares were unaffected, Bernama said.
The agency quoted Ling as saying that the government only controlled ticket prices for domestic routes while the international fares were "open to competition".
However, the government wanted to ensure any price increase would be within the reach of "ordinary people", he added.
Ling said a price increase on international routes was unavoidable because the cost of aircraft, jet-fuel, salaries and airline operations had increased over the past several years.
